title: pm: land low-risk skills wording on the seat's review (Tier S arm on the catalog rows)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XUhUNUU87zF4e1oTQPE9zim)_

Fixes #33501

domain:skills#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pF46HJnpBrhgVWtwV

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:登记表里 `skills/**` 与 `ui/skills/**` 两行仍是 Tier H,但多了一个「低风险技能臂」读数。以下全部成立才读成 Tier S:受管路径只在这两行;这两行下只有 `.md` 与 `evals/*.json`;其余路径只有 changeset 与 `docs/`、`content/docs/` 下的 Markdown 散文;正文恰好一行裸写的 `Clause-②: no` 和一行 `Metadata-protocol: none`(引用、代码块、尾随文字、多行声明都算 H);至少一个 changeset,在 head 读出,只发布 `'@objectstack/skills': patch`,也带这两行;不带 `security` 标签,时间线上也没被摘掉过;目录内路径名不含 security/auth/permission;目录内文件只能是「修改」的普通文件,且新旧模式相同(新增、删除、改名、复制、软链、改模式都算 H);不是 fork。合并队列守卫在 merge_group 腿读这些,再要求同 head 的达档复核记录写的是 PASS,席位入队才放行;`--pr` 预检给同一判定。AGENTS.md 第 14 条与 pm-dispatch 两处落地行同步;复核简报写明:路径名看不出的安全内容由复核记录写明、采纳记录的席位加 `security` 标签(带 `--paths` 且命中技能路径时无条件,不带 `--paths` 时以条件句出现)。
- 为什么改:你 2026-11-14 同意把低风险 Tier H 放权给座位(「同意 把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位」「把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位，立 p1 卡优化」);现在座位入队技能措辞 PR 会被必需检查 Governed Surface Queue Guard 弹出。
- 风险与回滚:上面任一条不成立或读不到(正文、标签、时间线、changeset、fork 判定),一律仍是 Tier H(失败即关);复核记录是 FAIL 或没写结论也拒。CODEOWNERS、`--test`、`--branch` 与中继请审照旧按路径读 H。`docs/adr/**` 不动,仍 Tier H,ADR 那一半由 #33539 承接。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看:`scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs` 的 `lowRiskArmVerdict` 与 `readBareDeclaration`;`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` 的 `readLowRiskTier` 与 `lowRiskRecordVerdict`;AGENTS.md 第 14 条 Tier S 括号。
- 两分钟验证:`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 33394`,预期 exit 3、`Tier S(席内达档复核落地)` 与 `low-risk skills arm ... Tier S` 一行。
- 需要你做的:本 PR 改 `AGENTS.md`,本身是 Tier H:请合并(或批准后由席位落地)。

## What changes

- **The register (`scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`).** The `skills-catalog` and `ui-skills-catalog` rows keep `tier: H` and gain `lowRisk` (scoped to objectstack), modelled on the workflows split: a READING moves them, the row does not. `lowRiskArmVerdict(matched, repo, reading)` reads Tier S only when ALL of these hold, each a printed reason when it does not:
  - every governed row hit is a catalog row;
  - every changed path lies under a hit catalog row or matches `LOW_RISK_RIDER_PATTERNS` (a `.changeset/*.md`, or Markdown prose under `docs/` or `content/docs/`), and every path under a catalog row is `.md` or `evals/*.json` (`LOW_RISK_ARM_FILE_PATTERNS`);
  - the body carries exactly one bare `Clause-②: no` and one bare `Metadata-protocol: none`. `readBareDeclaration` runs the fleet's own readers (`readClause2Line`, `readMetadataProtocolLine`) line by line, never a second parser: a second declaration, trailing words, an arm, or the line quoted or inside a fence is H;
  - at least one changeset, each read at the head, whose frontmatter releases nothing but `'@objectstack/skills': patch` (an empty frontmatter is allowed) and whose body carries the same two bare lines (`lowRiskChangesetReasons`);
  - the labels were read and none is `security`, and the timeline was read and has no `unlabeled` event for `security`;
  - `forkVerdict` of the pull object reads a same-repository head;
  - no catalog path names security, auth or permission (`LOW_RISK_SECURITY_NAME`, any case, any segment below the catalog row). Ruling-ref: card #33501 comment 6888245932, item 1 (Leehom, option B 「标签和路径都读」): the label OR the path sends the PR to H. A segment rather than the basename, because a skill folder named for security has `SKILL.md` as its entry file; a security word in a rider path (`docs/**`) is not read. On `main` five catalog files match, all basenames: `skills/objectstack-api/evals/endpoints-auth-routes.json`, `skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`, `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`, `skills/objectui/evals/auth-permissions.json`, `skills/objectui/guides/auth-permissions.md`;
  - every catalog path is a MODIFIED regular file with the same mode at both ends (`catalogFiles`, each row `{ path, status, oldMode, mode }`): an added, deleted, renamed or copied skill or eval, a symlink or submodule at either end (mode other than `100644`/`100755`), any mode change (a symlink turned regular file, or `100644` to `100755`), or a status or mode that was not read is H. Ruling-ref: card #33501 comment 6888245932, item 2 (Leehom, option A 「先补三项再合并」, item B).

  No reading, or an unmeasured one, is Tier H with its reason. `applyLowRiskArm` runs after `applyWorkflowSplit`, so a split workflow row beside a catalog path counts as a governed row outside the arm. `governedTierFor` and `testVerdict` take the reading as one more optional argument; every caller that passes none answers exactly as before (catalog paths Tier H). `renderLowRiskLines` prints the arm's verdict. `--pr` builds the reading from the pull object and file walk it already fetches (`pullLowRiskReading`), plus the timeline over the same channel (`fetchTimelineOver`, only when a catalog path is hit, every page or NOT MEASURED) and each changeset at the PR's head from this checkout (`pullChangesetReading`, NOT MEASURED with the fetch that cures it when the head is not here). `--pr` also reads each file's status off the API's file walk (`pullCatalogStatuses`; a rename's old name reads `renamed`, a copy's source `copied source`, never `modified`) and each modified catalog file's mode at the merge base and at the head from this checkout (`pullCatalogReading`, `git ls-tree`; a base or head not here, or no merge base, is NOT MEASURED, and the hint names the fetch: `pull/N/head` and the PR's own base ref, or its sha when the ref was not read, never an assumed `main` (`pullFetchHint`, which the workflow split's reading now shares)), since the API can call a symlink replaced by a regular file `modified`. `--test` and `--branch` have no body and say NOT MEASURED. The header section "The low-risk skills arm" lists the conditions.
- **The queue guard (`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs`).** `decomposeGovernedWork` keeps `allPaths` (every path of every attributed commit of the PR, collected before the governed filter drops a row) and `changesetRefs` (each changeset with the commit that touched it, ungoverned commits included). The entry reads the arm NOT MEASURED there; the `pull_request` leg prints Tier H with that note and never reddens. On `merge_group`, `readLowRiskTier` re-reads each catalog entry's tier through the register's `governedTierFor` with: the body, label names and `forkVerdict` of the pull object the leg already fetched (`makePullReader` now returns `labels` and `fork`); the timeline the enqueue leg already read (kept, not re-fetched; an unread or failed timeline is NOT MEASURED); each changeset by `git show <commit>:<path>`, and each governed commit's status and both modes per path by `git diff-tree -r --raw -z --no-renames` against its first parent (`catalogFilesOf`, the raw line's old and new mode; an add in one commit and an edit in the next reads `added`). Then the Tier S record leg runs, and for an entry the arm put at Tier S the same-head record must also READ PASS: `lowRiskRecordVerdict` reads the comment the locator chose with the fleet's `contractReviewVerdictOf`. FAIL, no verdict word, or no reader loaded is a refusal (`not-pass`) with its own line. A record carried from an older head (the regeneration and prose-only carry) stands for the arm only when the hops, diffed with the leg's git reader (`--no-renames`, so a rename lists both paths), moved no `.changeset/` path and no path under a catalog row (the carry admits both as prose, yet the arm reads its tier from them); an unreadable diff refuses. The other Tier S legs are unchanged and still read no verdict (#33541).
- **`scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs`.** Re-exports `contractReviewVerdictOf` from `check-half-states.mjs` (already its import), so the guard's lazy loader reaches the fleet's one verdict reader. The reviewer brief (`--brief-template`, `contractReviewBriefLines`) gains a `Security —` line: when the change teaches security, auth or permission behaviour the path name doesn't show, the record says so and the seat adopting the record adds the `security` label (ruling item 1; an isolated reviewer cannot label). Built with `--paths`, it prints when a `hits` path sits under a low-risk catalog row (`lowRiskRowHit`) and not otherwise. Built without `--paths` (the bare `--brief-template` that `contract-review.md` and `coordinator.md` teach), it prints in a conditional form, "if a `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`", on every at-tier face except the narrowing.
- **`AGENTS.md` Prime Directive 14.** The surface list drops "all Tier H"; Tier H is "every register row outside Tier S"; Tier S names `.claude/**` and the objectstack workflow edits and skills-only wording the register reads as S (`readWorkflowDiff`, `lowRiskArmVerdict`). It also names the duty for security teaching the name test cannot see (a file such as `relationships.md`): the seat adopting the review's record labels it `security` ("the seat labels unnamed security teaching"). To fit the 120-byte budget in the same 16 lines, the paragraph is re-wrapped and four phrases are shortened without changing a rule: "every register row outside Tier S" to "every row outside Tier S", ", and objectstack" to ", objectstack", "then lands it" to "lands it", "carries no information about" to "says nothing about". The detail lives in the script header, per AGENTS.md's own rule. Net content is 13 bytes shorter; the paragraph is re-wrapped at the 120-byte budget and keeps its 16 lines (AGENTS.md 1050 to 1050).
- **pm-dispatch.** `SKILL.md`: "路径面命中 Tier H" becomes "定档 Tier H", and the workflows line names both readings and keeps the workflow Tier H triggers (`readWorkflowDiff`(发布面/C2/拒读⇒H),技能 `lowRiskArmVerdict`,未读⇒H), within the 120-byte line budget. `references/lanes/skills.md`: the pre-arm check is `check-governed-merges --pr N` (only `--pr` can read the arm). The other places the card and comment 6885437809 listed were read and still hold as written: `contract-review.md` 16 and 51 and `landing-operations.md` 12 and 89 speak of Tier S and Tier H generically, `execution-duties.md` 17's soft cap already counts only PRs that stay Tier H, and `coordinator.md` names no tier.

## Why

Ruling-ref: Leehom, project chat 2026-11-14, verbatim 「同意 把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位」, then 「把低风险的 Tier H 放权给座位，立 p1 卡优化」. Measured on `origin/main` f068cde8: `GOVERNED_SURFACES` put `skills/**` at Tier H, and the guard's `merge_group` leg passes a Tier H entry only on an authorized approval or enqueue (`GOVERNED_APPROVERS`), so a seat enqueue of a skills wording PR is refused. Comment 6885437809 measured that the ruleset requires no review (PRs merged with zero reviews), so the guard is the only stop and no settings change is owed.

## Acceptance notes

- **`docs/adr/**` stays Tier H.** The ruling names ADR notes, but a path cannot tell a note from a changed decision. #33539 carries the ADR half of the ruling (an add-only note reading).
- **The relay's review plan still summons the approvers** (`scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs` `governedReviewPlan` reads paths only): a summons, not a block. Follow-up #33540.
- **The other Tier S legs of the queue guard still read no verdict** (`.claude/**`, the workflow split): only the low-risk arm requires PASS here. Follow-up #33541.
- **The reviewer's labelling duty is in PD 14 and in the review brief, not in `SKILL.md`, `references/lanes/skills.md` or `references/contract-review.md`.** Those three are at their ruled line ceilings with no headroom; adding the duty there costs a line in each, which needs a cut the seat chooses or a ceiling ruling. PD 14 binds every seat, and the brief hands the duty to the reviewer itself.
- **PD 14 does not quote the ruling or list the conditions** (review nit N1, not taken). `AGENTS.md`'s own rule allows no ruling date or quotation there (provenance cites a ruling record), and its line ceiling has no headroom. The conditions and the ruling live in the script header and the `lowRiskArmVerdict` docblock, which PD 14 names.
- **Tier evidence first.** Per ruling item 2 (C), the tier-evidence script (#33605, PR #33616) lands before this PR goes to the maintainer.
- **Not in this PR:** the `-z` gap in `enumerateRows` (it predates this PR) goes to its own card, #33620.
- **`--test` and `--branch` always read the arm NOT MEASURED** (they have no PR body); the seat's pre-arm check for a skills PR is `--pr N`.
- **Shared file with #33484:** `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` (two different lines). Whichever lands second merges `origin/main`.
- **Live readings** on two PRs waiting for a click: `--pr 33394` and `--pr 33482` both still read Tier S through the tightened arm (timeline, fork and changesets read; head fetched locally). They still need a same-head `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS record before the seat enqueues, and they can only use the arm once this PR is on `main`.

## Verification

Head `60e5e255` (after the at-tier reviews 6886787995, 6887175399, 6887454202, 6887748912, 6888217778 and 6888563583, whose SF5, N11 and N12 this head answers; branch merged with `origin/main`, which brought other lines of `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` and no other file this PR touches).

<details><summary>Self-tests of the edited scripts</summary>

- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, 690 assertions. Battery "⚖️ the low-risk skills arm" now 74 cases (floor pinned at 74), pinning each review item: M1 (no changeset; changesets unread; another package, `minor`/`major`, or a second release line; changeset missing or annotating either declaration; no frontmatter; not readable at the head; a changed changeset the reading holds no file for; body without a bare `Metadata-protocol: none`; the catalog at patch in either quote or an empty frontmatter is S), S1 (`unlabeled` security in any case; another label removed stays S; timeline unread or not a list; `--pr` reads the timeline only when a catalog path is hit), S2 (trailing words; two declarations, even two `no`; a quoted or fenced `no` before a real `yes`, backtick and tilde fences; a lone fenced or quoted `no`; a closed fence before the real line stays S), S3 (fork; deleted head repo; unread fork predicate), S4 (`.js`, `.json` outside `evals/`, nested `evals/sub/*.json`, `.yaml`, `.png`, `.sh` are H; `evals/*.json` is S), the security name test (a matching `.md` and `evals/*.json`, all five files on `main`, any case, the `ui/skills/**` catalog, a skill folder named for it, a rename into and out of such a name, a rider path not read), the modified-file rule (added, deleted on either spelling, renamed both sides, added then modified, symlink, mode or status not read; `100755` at both ends and an added rider stay S), N10 (a symlink turned regular file called `modified` is H on its base mode; `100644` to `100755` and back are H; a base mode not read is H; a copy's source reads `copied source` and H), plus `pullChangesetReading`, `pullCatalogStatuses`, `pullCatalogReading` (merge-base and head modes; base not here, no base sha, or no merge base is NOT MEASURED; the fetch hint names the base sha when no ref was read and the base ref, such as `release/v4`, when it was; its symlink-at-base reading drives the arm to H) and `lowRiskRowHit`.
- `node scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, 487 cases. Battery "⚖️ the low-risk skills arm at the queue" now 54 cases (floor 54), end to end through `runGuard` on `merge_group`: the PASS clear; a PASS record carried over a docs-only hop clears, while one carried over a hop that rewrote the changeset or moved a skill's `CHANGELOG.md` is refused, as is a carried record whose hops cannot be diffed; the carry check's diff carries `--no-renames` (argument pinned), and on a real temporary repository (every git call under `gitFreeEnv()` with `-c commit.gpgsign=false`; the self-test also passes with `GIT_DIR` set to a bogus path) a skill renamed out of the catalog into `content/docs/` refuses the carried record while the plain diff names only the destination, and a rename into `permission-guide.md` lists both sides, refuses the carry naming both, and reads H through the name test; a security-named file, a rename into or out of such a name, a skill added or deleted in the group, a rename as delete plus add, a symlink, a symlink turned regular file (old mode `120000`, as `M` or as `T`), a regular file made executable, and a status read that throws or misses the path each stay H with a PASS record; `catalogFilesOf` reads status and both modes per commit; a same-head FAIL record, a record with no verdict word, a newer FAIL behind an older PASS, and a recogniser set without the verdict reader are each refused (`not-pass`); `**VERDICT: PASS**` clears; a non-arm Tier S entry with a FAIL record still stands (unchanged, #33541); M1, S1, S2, S3, S4 each H with a valid PASS record (changeset in another commit of the PR included; no git reader; a timeline that threw or was never read); `makePullReader` carries the fork predicate.
- `node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --self-test`: exit 0, 386 cases. Battery "letter C" 19 to 22: the brief over a `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` path (beside other paths, and through the `--brief-template --paths` CLI) carries the duty unconditionally, with the seat adding the label; the bare brief, `--face rules` and `--face schema` (function and CLI) carry it in the conditional form; a known path list off the arm, the declaration face and the narrowing face carry none.
- Mutation checks (not kept, each restored): dropping the PASS check, ignoring the guard's timeline, ignoring the guard's fork reading, ignoring `unlabeled`, allowing a second declaration, allowing a fenced line, switching S4 off, allowing no changeset, skipping the carried-record check, dropping `--no-renames`, switching off the security name test, switching off the status test (on either leg), dropping the brief line or printing it on every brief, ignoring a mode change, reading the head mode only, reading the base mode at the head, the guard reading the new mode as the old, carrying a copy's source as `renamed`, dropping the brief's conditional form, wording the line as the reviewer adding the label, and a fetch hint naming `main` or only the base sha each turn the self-test red.

</details>

<details><summary>Derived gates: 47 derived, 47 run, all exit 0</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 47 families on head `60e5e255` (`check:pm-record-recognisers` among them, for the re-export and the brief line). Each ran with its exit code captured before any pipe, after building `@objectstack/lint...` under the verify lock (VERDICT command-exit 0). All 47 exit 0. `--ran`: "47 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 47 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)". CI families are read from this PR's check-runs, not re-run here.

</details>

<details><summary>Tier, governed reading, line budget</summary>

- `dispatch-gates --tier`: MANDATORY contract-review tier, from `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`.
- `node scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`: exit 0. `SKILL.md` stays 319 lines; its workflows line is exactly 120 bytes and the tier line says the skills arm is exclusive. `AGENTS.md` stays 1050 lines; PD 14's last eight lines are re-wrapped at the byte budget for "skills-only".
- Live on head `0fbe225c`: `--pr 33394` and `--pr 33482` read Tier S through the arm, with the timeline, fork, changesets and both file modes (merge base and head) read (heads fetched locally).

</details>
